ei.title: Sharing as Insurance in the Ache Tribe
ei.subject: 수능특강

fullPassage: Hunters in the Ache tribe, living in the Paraguayan jungle, have a lot of ups and downs in their success at the hunt. Some days they bring home much more food than they could possibly eat; other days they come home empty-handed. If a man caught a wild pig and hoarded it for himself and his family, much of it would go to waste (there are no deep-freeze refrigerators in the Paraguayan jungle). Instead of living by a philosophy of "rugged individualism," however, hunters who have a lucky day share their meat with other families. During unlucky periods, individual hunters and their families would starve. And they don't just share a little; they share a lot — fully 90%. In exchange for this generosity, their neighbors share with them on days when the luck runs the other way. By exchanging resources, particularly those that are unpredictable and uncertain (like meat from the hunt, as opposed to vegetable crops), the group provides a mutual insurance policy against starvation.

questions.passage: Hunters in the Ache tribe, living in the Paraguayan jungle, have a lot of ups and downs in their success at the hunt. Some days they bring home much more food than they could possibly eat; other days they come home (A)[empty-handed / well-equipped]. If a man caught a wild pig and hoarded it for himself and his family, much of it would go to (B)[waste / use] (there are no deep-freeze refrigerators in the Paraguayan jungle). Instead of living by a philosophy of "rugged individualism," however, hunters who have a lucky day share their meat with other families. During unlucky periods, individual hunters and their families would starve. And they don't just share a little; they share a lot — fully 90%. In exchange for this (C)[generosity / selfishness], their neighbors share with them on days when the luck runs the other way. By exchanging resources, particularly those that are unpredictable and uncertain (like meat from the hunt, as opposed to vegetable crops), the group provides a mutual insurance policy against starvation.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① well-equipped: '잘 준비된'은 사냥 실패 맥락과 반대
❌ ② use/selfishness: 음식이 '쓰이다'와 '이기심'은 원문과 반대
❌ ③ well-equipped/selfishness: 둘 다 원문과 불일치
✅ ④ empty-handed - waste - generosity = 원문 일치 ←정답
det.tip: empty-handed=빈손으로, waste=낭비, generosity=관대함

Instead of living by a philosophy of "(A)[rugged / cooperative] individualism," however, hunters who have a lucky day share their meat with other families. ❌ ③ consistent: '일관된' 자원은 '예측 불가능한'이라는 원문과 반대

questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 policy의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

❌ ③ (A) 정책/(B) 원칙: '원칙'은 보험이 아님
❌ ④ (A) 원칙/(B) 보험: 회사 맥락에서 '원칙'보다 '정책'이 정확
det.tip: policy: (A) 정책/방침(company policy) vs (B) 보험(insurance policy)

questions.passage: Hunters in the Ache tribe, living in the Paraguayan jungle, have a lot of ups and downs in their success at the hunt. Some days they bring home much more food than they could possibly eat; other days they come home empty-handed. If a man caught a wild pig and __________ it for himself and his family, much of it would go to waste (there are no deep-freeze refrigerators in the Paraguayan jungle). Instead of living by a philosophy of "rugged individualism," however, hunters who have a lucky day share their meat with other families. During unlucky periods, individual hunters and their families would starve. And they don't just share a little; they share a lot — fully 90%. In exchange for this generosity, their neighbors share with them on days when the luck runs the other way. By exchanging resources, particularly those that are unpredictable and uncertain (like meat from the hunt, as opposed to vegetable crops), the group provides a mutual insurance policy against starvation.
